acceptanceCriteria: The target proposal is human-reviewable, links this handoff and both baselines, and contains no unrelated contract change.
avmRequirements: Run the target repository formatting, lint, documentation, examples, test, and AVM pattern-module compliance checks.
compatibilityConstraints: Preserve existing Terraform inputs and outputs; use a reviewed deprecation transition before any removal.
defaultBehavior: Preserve existing Terraform defaults unless a documented migration and semantic-version decision explicitly changes them.
Bicep creates private DNS only when isolated and defaults to module ownership; Terraform creates or references private zones as part of its mandatory private topology.
Bicep networkIsolation defaults false; Terraform service public network defaults are mostly false while private endpoints are always created.
Terraform private_endpoints_manage_dns_zone_group defaults true; Bicep policyManagedPrivateDns defaults false and applies across local zone/group creation.

standalone-network-isolated: Require a separate successful approved test deployment plus reviewed DNS, endpoint, reachability, RBAC, and isolation comparison for this scenario.
standalone-standard: Static checks and plan are non-parity evidence; require a successful approved test deployment and reviewed capability comparison for this scenario.

exclusions: Do not implement hub-spoke or arbitrary optional-feature combinations in this proposal unless separately reviewed.
identityRequirements: Prefer managed identity; preserve inventory identity behavior and do not introduce credentials.
Cross-subscription hub peering requires operator permissions outside the spoke deployment.
Gateway identity receives certificate-secret access only when live TLS ingress is configured.
Jumpbox receives explicit managed identity and scoped operational roles when deployed.
migrationPlan: No consumer migration is intended; reject implementation choices that require one and return for review.
networkingRequirements: Preserve scenario-specific public access, private endpoint, DNS, route, subnet, delegation, and dependency-ordering behavior recorded by the inventory.
Bicep can create, reuse, or defer DNS zone groups to policy; shared-zone links are explicitly consumer-owned when BYO IDs are used.
Bicep creates private endpoints only when networkIsolation is true and preserves service dependency ordering.
Bicep isolated defaults derive Bastion and NAT from jumpbox selection; standard deploys none by default.
Container Apps Environment delegation and private endpoint network policies are part of the subnet contract.
Empty source prefixes keep the default-off gateway skeleton inert; explicit sources and certificate activate HTTPS.
Network-isolated standalone routes workload subnets through local or supplied egress and controls allowed destinations explicitly.
standalone-network-isolated has a VNet, private endpoints, firewall, Bastion, NAT, and private DNS.
standalone-standard has public access and no mandatory VNet, private endpoints, firewall, Bastion, NAT, or private DNS.
The reverse hub-to-spoke peering remains operator/platform-owned in the Bicep contract.
rbacRequirements: Apply least-privilege RBAC and preserve explicit control-plane and data-plane role boundaries.
Cross-subscription hub peering requires operator permissions outside the spoke deployment.
Gateway identity receives certificate-secret access only when live TLS ingress is configured.
Jumpbox receives explicit managed identity and scoped operational roles when deployed.
requiredBehavior: Hub/spoke peering and gateway transit: Optional spoke-to-hub peering, route ownership, gateway transit, and remote gateway controls.
Jumpbox, Bastion, and NAT Gateway: Independent nullable component flags, legacy deployVM fallback, BYO IDs, Bastion access/SKU/tunneling, and VM configuration.
NSGs, routes, firewall, and egress rules: NSG deployment, Azure Firewall/UDR egress, media egress, bootstrap/build FQDN extensions, and existing or external next-hop routes.
Private DNS creation, BYO zones, policy ownership, and links: Policy-managed DNS, fifteen granular BYO private-zone IDs, link suffixing, zone groups, and link ownership.
Private endpoint location, resource group, ordering, and service coverage: Private endpoint placement, subnet use, DNS zone groups, and serialized dependencies for all supported services.
Optional Application Gateway WAF ingress: Default-off aggregate public ingress, WAF, TLS, allow-list, identity, subnet, and automation outputs.

Standard versus network-isolated standalone topology: The networkIsolation=false public baseline and networkIsolation=true VNet/private endpoint/firewall/Bastion/NAT/private DNS baseline are distinct and assessed independently.
VNet, subnet names, prefixes, delegation, and existing VNet: All VNet/subnet name and address surfaces, existing-VNet reuse, and subnet deployment controls.

standalone-network-isolated: standalone-network-topology: partial - The broad private shape exists, but Terraform has no networkIsolation contract and service-level access controls differ.
virtual-network-and-subnets: partial - Terraform supports created/BYO VNet and subnet maps, but names, defaults, delegation, and side-by-side semantics differ.
network-security-routing-firewall: partial - Terraform has NSG/firewall/route definitions but lacks Bicep's jumpbox/build/media egress presets and existing-route-table contract.
hub-peering-integration: partial - Terraform supports VNet/vWAN peering but uses a different aggregate contract and ownership model.
private-dns-ownership: partial - Terraform supports created/existing/policy-linked zones, but namespace coverage, defaults, link naming, and ownership differ.
private-endpoint-placement: partial - Terraform creates private endpoints but does not expose equivalent cross-region/resource-group placement and ordering controls.
jumpbox-bastion-nat: partial - Terraform has jump VM and Bastion definitions but no equivalent independent NAT/BYO/legacy fallback contract.
public-application-gateway-ingress: partial - Terraform exposes Application Gateway/WAF definitions but not the same aggregate activation semantics and output set.
standalone-standard: standalone-network-topology: blocked - Consumers cannot request the Bicep public, no-VNet standalone shape. Terraform v0.5.1 always creates Foundry private endpoints and requires VNet/subnet inputs; its service defaults disable public access, so networkIsolation=false has no analogue.

virtual-network-and-subnets: blocked - Terraform requires VNet and subnet structure even though Bicep standard requires none. Required Terraform vnet_definition and always-created private endpoints prevent a no-VNet standalone-standard deployment.

network-security-routing-firewall: blocked - Terraform introduces routes and private network controls absent from standard. Terraform's required private network means its routing and firewall choices cannot yield Bicep's no-mandatory-network standalone-standard topology.

hub-peering-integration: blocked - This optional integration does not create a standard topology in Terraform. Terraform still requires its spoke VNet and private endpoints; peering options cannot remove them for standalone-standard.

private-dns-ownership: blocked - Terraform mandates private endpoint DNS behavior where standard needs no private DNS. Mandatory Terraform private endpoints require private DNS decisions, unlike Bicep standalone-standard's public topology.

private-endpoint-placement: blocked - Terraform private endpoints cannot be disabled to obtain the public standard baseline. Foundry create_private_endpoints=true and required private endpoint subnet structure make private endpoints structural in Terraform v0.5.1.

jumpbox-bastion-nat: blocked - Even with Terraform jump resources disabled, mandatory VNet/private endpoints remain. Terraform cannot remove the underlying private topology to produce standalone-standard; jumpbox/Bastion flags do not change that constraint.

public-application-gateway-ingress: blocked - Terraform Application Gateway exists only with its required private landing-zone topology. Terraform's Application Gateway option cannot be combined with a no-VNet/no-private-endpoint standard deployment.

securityInvariants: Do not store secrets, private environment values, or claim effective isolation from static inspection.
